newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Shaken dollar stabilises, Eurostocks steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Shaken dollar stabilises, Eurostocks steady.

text.p: A badly shaken dollar regained some poise on Monday after tumbling about six yen since Friday, while London stocks slipped slightly despite news of a major merger in the drinks business.
Traders said the dollar had found solid support at 118 yen and the market was now awaiting more data on the U.S. and Japanese economies before deciding which way to move.

In equities, London slipped on light profit taking despite a big boost from a proposed merger of Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc. The deal, worth more than 20 billion pounds ($33 billion), would create the world's seventh biggest food and drinks group.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar recovered to 118.85 yen by midday after sliding to 117.50 yen, its lowest since January, in Tokyo. But it was still well below the 120.08 seen in European trade late on Friday.
Traders said relief after the dollar found solid support at 118 yen caused a slight bounce, although the U.S. currency still looked far from robust.

The dollar was helped by comments from senior Japanese officials earlier in the day. These were seen as an attempt to stem its slide, triggered late last week by uncertainties over U.S. and Japanese interest rates.
A weaker yen helps Japanese exporters but also increases friction with Washington over the Japanese trade surplus.

Japanese authorities, who during the dollar's recent rally had been expressing worries about the yen's "excessive" weakness, were content to see dollar/yen falling. But they had not been prepared to see it crumble quite so rapidly, analysts said.
"The Japanese officials are worried. They didn't want the dollar to suddenly collapse like this," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London.
"All they wanted to do was stop the uptrend. They didn't want it to come back down as there's no benefit in Japan seeing a weaker dollar at the moment."

U.S. and Japanese interest rates have been the driving force behind the dollar's recent surge. But late last week U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan appeared to hint that he was now less inclined to raise rates to counter possible inflation.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the central bank's policy-making arm, is due to consider U.S. rates on May 20.
Dollar/mark was sidelined for most of the morning as all eyes were riveted to the crumbling dollar/yen, but it was dampened by comments from Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen.
By midday, the dollar was at 1.6925 marks compared with 1.6843 late on Friday.

On stocks, investors could not resist the temptation to take some light profits in London despite news of the merger of Grand Met and Guinness. But after earlier dipping a few points, the FTSE index was down only 1.7 points at 4,629.2 by midday.
"A bit of profit-taking was inevitable," said Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International. "But people are still buying on the dips so I wouldn't look for any big setback."
The FTSE rose 175 points last week, and has gained 379 points or nine percent since April 15.
Shares in the companies involved in the merger leapt. Guinness was up 93-1/2 pence to 610 and Grand Met gained 91 to 606.

In Paris shares in drinks and luxury goods company LVMH also jumped 4.21 percent to 1,436 francs. Traders said LVMH would benefit from a reevaluation of its stake in Guinness and the merger with Grand Met could open up new outlets for LVMH brands.
The merger raised spirits throughout the Paris market with the CAC-40 index rising 31.36 points or 1.19 percent to 2,665.27.

The market was also buoyed by opinion polls which seemed to reassure investors that the ruling centre-right parties were holding their lead over the Socialists for elections at the end of this month and in June.
The German market recovered from an early dip despite the dollar's weakness, which hurts German exporters. The DAX index was up 3.31 points at 3,565.72.
Dealers reported selctive buying, notably of Deutsche Telekom which was up 1.24 marks at 41.19 on generally positive sentiment before its annual news conference on Tuesday.
STOCK PRICES AT 1045 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 1.7 points at 4,629.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 31.36 points (1.19 percent) to 2,665.27.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 3.31 points at 3,565.72.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6925 marks compared with 1.6843 late in Europe on Friday and 118.85 yen versus 120.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $348.20 an ounce after closing at $346.20 in London on Friday. Silver was down one cent at $4.86.
($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
